title: Security & Governance
decisionRationale: All critical and high findings uncovered by the RC-3 defensive pass are remediated with executable evidence (migration applied, RLS policies verified via pg_policies). Remaining medium findings are either accepted with documented compensating controls or already tracked as RC-1 operator gates. The 4 RC-1 operator gates (rate-limit adapter, Google OAuth, API bearer rotation, baseline backup) remain open per instruction; GA is NOT claimed and RC-4 is NOT started.
openOperatorGatesFromRC1: Google OAuth provider enabled in Cloud
APIC-001 demo bearer retired; production APIClient rows provisioned

findings.title: audit_events SELECT policy exposed cross-tenant history to any authenticated user
findings.evidenceBefore: pg_policies: audit_events "audit read" qual = true (any authenticated caller could SELECT every audit row from every workspace).
findings.impact: Cross-tenant leakage of governance history: actors, actions, redacted-but-structured payloads, correlation IDs, workspaces.
findings.remediation: Migration 20260717235000: DROP + CREATE POLICY "audit read" USING (has_role(auth.uid(),'owner') OR actor = auth.uid()). Owners retain full visibility; other authenticated users only see rows they themselves emitted. App-layer audit views already filter by workspace on top of this.
findings.evidenceAfter: pg_policies: audit_events "audit read" qual = (has_role(auth.uid(), 'owner'::app_role) OR (actor = auth.uid())). Verified via psql.
findings.residualRisk: Owner role sees all workspaces' audit rows (by design for compliance). Non-owner users can still see their own action history across workspaces they participated in — considered acceptable for the actor's own accountability trail.

findings.title: audit_events INSERT allowed actor forgery
findings.evidenceBefore: pg_policies: audit_events "audit insert" with_check = (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL). Any signed-in caller could INSERT audit rows claiming any actor UUID, corrupting the accountability trail.
findings.impact: Integrity of the append-only ledger relied entirely on client-side hash chaining; a hostile authenticated caller could inject rows attributed to another user (the DB chain-hash column is under caller control on INSERT).
findings.remediation: Migration 20260717235000: DROP + CREATE POLICY "audit insert" WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND (actor IS NULL OR actor = auth.uid())). Non-null actor must match the caller; system rows may use NULL actor. Append-only guaranteed by absence of UPDATE/DELETE policies.
findings.evidenceAfter: pg_policies: with_check = ((auth.uid() IS NOT NULL) AND ((actor IS NULL) OR (actor = auth.uid()))). Verified via psql.
findings.residualRisk: Callers can still emit rows attributed to themselves with arbitrary payload; chain-hash verification (src/lib/data/audit.ts::verifyAuditChain) plus workspace filtering detects/quarantines anomalous chains.

findings.title: profiles SELECT exposed every user's email to any authenticated user
findings.evidenceBefore: pg_policies: profiles "profiles readable by authenticated" qual = true. Any authenticated caller could SELECT email + display_name for the entire user base.
findings.impact: PII (email) enumeration by any signed-in user; violates least-privilege for a directory whose UI needs only display_name/avatar for author bylines.
findings.remediation: Migration 20260717235000: (a) rewrote SELECT policy set — "profiles self or owner read" grants full-row read to self and owners, "profiles public directory" retains USING (true) for display_name/avatar; (b) revoked column-level SELECT on `profiles.email` from authenticated at the table level and re-granted only the non-email columns; email column privilege is present but only satisfies the self/owner policy for non-owners.
findings.evidenceAfter: pg_policies + \dp public.profiles confirm split policies; authenticated column grants exclude broad email exposure. `profiles self insert`, `profiles self update` policies retained.
findings.residualRisk: Owners can enumerate all emails (required for admin surfaces). App-layer directory endpoints must not SELECT email for cross-user queries — repository already projects display_name/avatar only for public byline paths.

findings.title: Content tables (concepts, knowledge_objects, domains, frameworks, publications, releases, agents, prompts, client_tools, review_items, qa_issues, relationships, revisions) SELECT policies do not enforce workspace scoping at the DB layer
findings.evidence: pg_policies: every content-table SELECT policy is USING (true). Workspace isolation is enforced only at the repository/service layer (src/lib/data/workspaces.ts::scopeEntities, workspace-scoping.ts, detectWorkspaceLeakage).
findings.impact: A caller bypassing app code (raw PostgREST calls with a valid bearer) could read cross-workspace content rows.
compensatingControls: Repository mutation boundary (src/lib/data/repository.ts::auditedMutate) rejects cross-workspace writes.
detectWorkspaceLeakage() runs in startupDiagnostics and hard-fails the deployment surface when foreign-workspace rows appear under the active workspace.
TanStack server functions (createServerFn + requireSupabaseAuth) mediate all first-party reads and stamp workspaceId filters before the SELECT is issued.
Public `/api/public/v1/*` endpoints route through resolveClient(), which stamps workspaceId from the APIClient row, and the pre-auth abuse bucket blocks credential-guessing.
findings.acceptedRisk: Introducing per-row workspace_id CHECK policies on ~13 tables during RC-3 is a schema-shape migration touching every repository call site; deferred to a dedicated multi-tenant hardening slice post-RC-3. Documented in ARCHITECTURE.md.

findings.title: Rate-limit adapter defaults to in-memory unless RATE_LIMIT_ADAPTER=supabase
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/rate-limit.ts::assertRateLimitReadiness returns { ok:false } when NODE_ENV=production without the Supabase adapter; startupDiagnostics surfaces FAIL and releaseCandidateReadiness marks BLOCKED.
findings.note: Fail-closed guard already implemented — no code change required.

findings.title: Seed APIClient APIC-001 must be retired before production traffic
findings.evidence: resolveClient() in src/routes/api/public/v1/$.ts only trusts APIC-001 when process.env.DEMO_API_KEY matches — not enabled in RC-1 env.

findings.title: CSP is default-src 'none' on API responses; app HTML routes rely on framework defaults
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/security.ts::securityHeaders() emits nosniff, DENY, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, restrictive Permissions-Policy, HSTS 2y, CSP default-src 'none'; used on JSON API responses via /api/public/v1.
findings.acceptedRisk: Full-app CSP nonce policy on SSR HTML responses is deferred; the app runs under HTTPS with framework defaults. HSTS + X-Frame-Options DENY are in effect on all API paths.

findings.title: Dependency audit not automated in CI
findings.evidence: bun.lock present; no scheduled audit job in this repo.
findings.acceptedRisk: Sandbox has no npm-audit surface; deferred to platform-level dependency scanning.

findings.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML in src/components/ui/chart.tsx
findings.evidence: Static shadcn/ui chart component injects CSS variables computed from typed ChartConfig; no user-controlled input reaches the sink.

findings.title: 6 SECURITY DEFINER helpers callable by anon/authenticated
findings.evidence: Supabase linter WARN 0028×2 + 0029×4 for has_role, has_any_role, workspace_role, is_workspace_member, consume_rate_limit, handle_new_user. Intentional per user-roles guidance and tanstack-supabase-integration — required for the RLS-bypass helper pattern.

findings.title: No secrets in client bundle
findings.evidence: grep -RIE 'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE|sb_secret_|service_role_key' dist/client → 2 matches, both string literals inside @supabase/auth-js library code (Solana web3 grant_type + provider constants). No JWT-shaped tokens found.

findings.title: No eval / new Function in src/
Audit chain integrity verifiable in-repo
findings.evidence: src/lib/data/audit.ts::verifyAuditChain returns { ok, brokenAt, count } across the ledger; deterministic SHA-256 via src/lib/data/security.ts::sha256Hex; regression coverage in scripts/validate.ts.

findings.title: Restore path is governed
findings.evidence: performGovernedRestore() requires typed 'RESTORE' confirmation + ≥8-char reason; takes a pre-restore backup of the current snapshot; verifyBackupIntegrity() re-hashes and rejects future-schema-version.
